move:
Create a production action-pose study of this EXACT preferred original ADULT MALE ALIEN HUNTER for an action RPG. The attached R08 original is the identity AND weapon reference, not a vague mood. Preserve grey ridged alien face, amber eyes, backward short bone head plates, broad powerful chest, exposed rough grey torso, diagonal cartridge bandolier and tooth trophy, asymmetrical worn silver/black/oxblood RIGHT shoulder armor and complete mechanical RIGHT arm, natural muscular LEFT arm, dark armored trousers with red thigh plates, heavy boots. Preserve the distinctive huge black/silver/oxblood SINGLE-BARREL revolver-rifle: very long barrel with dark-red inset, large CYLINDRICAL RECEIVER and squared surrounding support bracket, angular shoulder stock, same huge relative scale. Do not turn it into a pistol, machinegun, multi-barrel minigun, generic sniper rifle or rocket launcher. Clear connected rear grip and forward support point. Right mechanical hand on REAR TRIGGER GRIP, natural LEFT hand on FORE-END AHEAD of the big cylinder. Stock can contact RIGHT shoulder. Weapon order rear stock -> right grip -> cylinder -> left support -> long barrel. Maintain recognizable geometry while rotating it for the pose.

CAMERA FOR ALL ACTION STUDIES: game-style high three-quarter camera, looking down approximately 35 degrees; see head top, shoulders, chest and feet, not eye-level portrait. Character faces diagonally toward screen-right and lower-right, with near visible mechanical right arm. Single full character centered, 4:3 or square frame, 78 percent canvas height; ENTIRE barrel, stock, both feet, head and hands fully inside frame with generous margins. Plain matte medium charcoal background, subtle flat ground plane, soft grounded contact shadow. No scenery, grid text, labels, UI, layout panels or duplicate figures. Consistent neutral key light and restrained warm rim separate skin, matte fabric and worn metal. Premium game character concept illustration, clear large shapes, selective crisp edges, low microdetail noise. This is a single key pose for motion design, not a sprite-sheet or multiple-frame collage. Anatomy and mechanical continuity matter more than decorative effects.

ACTION 1 — COMBAT LOCOMOTION. Show the passing moment of a purposeful forward combat stride toward lower-right. Right leg advances and bears weight, left boot pushes off, natural readable stride, slight forward torso lean. The enormous rifle is carried LOW-READY diagonally down and forward toward screen-right, below sternum, muzzle safely clear of both legs. Right mechanical hand wraps rear grip, left hand supports fore-end, both elbows comfortably bent. Stock sits close under right shoulder, not floating behind neck. The upper body stabilizes the heavy weapon while legs move. Keep silhouette open: barrel distinct from forward boot, left forearm distinct from torso, amber-eyed alien face visible. No firing, no charge glow, no muzzle flash, no motion blur. The weight and arm ergonomics must look plausible for this very strong cyborg alien.

ACTION 2 — BASIC SHOT, RECOIL KEY POSE. Show one deliberate heavy shot directed diagonally toward screen-right/lower-right. Same high three-quarter game camera and original alien identity. Broad stable staggered stance with knees soft, forward natural LEFT foot toward aim, rear RIGHT foot bracing. Body turns into the line of aim, stock firmly touching RIGHT shoulder, mechanical RIGHT hand gripping rear grip and taking recoil, natural LEFT hand visibly supporting fore-end AHEAD of cylinder, not clamped onto the cylinder. Both hands must be readable and separate from weapon. Rifle raised into shoulder firing line, below and beside the face rather than blocking face. A small tight warm muzzle flash only at the ONE barrel tip, faint short smoke; weapon and elbows recoil backward slightly, not huge shoulder dislocation or airborne body. No laser beam, no excessive sparks, no charge aura. Emphasize a plausible complete chain from shoulder-stock to grip to cylinder to forward hand to barrel. Entire long barrel and stock in frame.

ACTION 3 — CHARGED SHOT, ANTICIPATION KEY POSE BEFORE FIRING. Same high three-quarter game camera and original alien identity. One enormous single barrel aimed diagonally toward screen-right/lower-right, face visible above gun. The huge central cylinder shows a controlled deep red light in a FEW existing recessed cartridge seams; small restrained red indicator at mechanical shoulder/forearm connects body and weapon. A tiny concentrated red glow inside barrel opening, no firing flash yet, no beam or explosion, no expanding magic circle. No floating magazine or impossible exposed mechanism. Preserve weapon outline from original; the posture, cylinder light and arm bracing should communicate charging at a small game-camera scale. Grounded believable compression in legs rather than random heroic kneeling.
rejectedFireCorrection: EDIT TARGET: this basic firing action study. Preserve the exact same original male grey bone-headed alien, materials, armor, mechanical RIGHT arm, natural LEFT arm, giant single-barrel cylindrical-receiver rifle and upper three-quarter camera. Make ONLY a production correction to the firing ergonomics and framing. Move the buttstock contact DOWN onto the RIGHT shoulder pocket at upper-chest height, leaving a clearly visible gap between the top of the stock and the underside of his jaw. The gun must not press into his mouth or throat. Slightly lift his chin and straighten his upper spine, keep eyes following target. Lower the entire weapon a little while retaining forward shoulder bracing: mechanical RIGHT hand on the rear pistol grip, natural LEFT hand ahead of cylinder under fore-end, both hands clearly separated. Maintain upright stable basic-shot stance, less crouched than a charged shot. One small tight muzzle flash, short faint smoke, no red glowing cylinder or charge indicators. Preserve the same full-body pose and weapon proportions as closely as possible. Pull back the camera enough to include the full muzzle flash and barrel tip with 8 percent clear image margin to the right and both full boots with ground beneath. Keep neutral charcoal studio ground and original light. Output one square finished action-study image. No additional figures, text or panels.
